guide.everyone.1: Banks and government entities never ask for your one-time code, PIN or password.
guide.everyone.2: Pause when a message rushes you. Scammers depend on speed.
guide.everyone.3: Verify through the official app or a number you already know — never through the message itself.
guide.seniors.1: If a caller claims to be the bank or police and asks for money or codes, hang up and call the official number.
guide.seniors.2: Never install an app because a caller asked you to.
guide.seniors.3: Saying "I will call you back" is always acceptable. Real institutions understand.
guide.students.1: Jobs that pay for likes or tasks but ask you to deposit money first are scams.
guide.students.2: Never let anyone use your bank account to receive money for them.
guide.students.3: Before logging in, read the real domain in the address bar, not the name in the message.
guide.families.1: Agree on a family safe word for emergencies — voices can be cloned with AI.
guide.families.2: A "new number" asking for urgent money? Call the old number first.
guide.families.3: Talk with children about gift-card and game-currency scams.

fp.title: Family safety plan
fp.why: AI can copy a voice. It can’t copy something your family never put online.
fp.word_rule: Agree it in person. Never type it in a group chat.
fp.word_how: Anyone calling for urgent help must say it.
fp.callback_how: Hang up and call the number already saved in your phone — caller ID can be faked.
fp.trusted_how: Before any urgent payment, check with them first.
fp.private_how: Fewer public videos means less material to clone a voice or face.
fp.bank_how: From the back of your card or the official app.
rc.title: If it already happened
rc.sub: Act in the first minutes — and only through official channels.
rc.s1_how: Use the number on the back of your card or the official app. Ask them to freeze the card or stop the transfer.
rc.s2_how: Abu Dhabi Police Aman works 24/7. Dubai Police eCrime and the My Safe Society app are listed on the UAE portal.
rc.s3_how: Change any password you shared, sign out other devices, and turn on two-step login.
rc.s4_how: Tell your family, and report the message to MIRGAB — reports are anonymised and reviewed before any warning is published.
rc.source: Channels from the UAE Government portal (u.ae) and Abu Dhabi Police. Check the official sites for the latest details.

ac.title: Detection accuracy
ac.overall: accuracy on {n} held-out messages and links
ac.lead: MIRGAB was tested on public data it had never seen: live phishing links, popular legitimate sites, a public SMS benchmark, and UAE scam scenarios in Arabic, Emirati dialect and English. Every number below can be re-run now on this server.
ac.running: Running all tests on this server…
ac.wait: Just ran — try again in a minute.
ac.nomatch: differs from the recorded results (the engine changed since they were recorded).
ac.method_1: Each public dataset was split 50/50 with a fixed seed. Improvements were tuned only on the first half; the numbers here come from the second half, which was never used for tuning.
ac.method_2: “Flagged” means MIRGAB shows a warning (risk level medium or higher) — exactly what a user sees.
ac.method_3: Phishing links are live URLs from the OpenPhish community feed; legitimate links are 1,000 sites spread across a public top-10,000 popularity list.
ac.method_4: The public SMS set labels marketing texts as “spam”; MIRGAB targets fraud, so its detection rate there understates fraud detection.
ac.method_5: The UAE set was written by the MIRGAB team from publicly reported UAE scam types and includes look-alike legitimate messages (real OTP texts, bank and delivery notices). It was not used for tuning, but it is small — treat it as indicative.
sh.qr_local: A QR code appears here on the public HTTPS link. This copy runs only on this computer (127.0.0.1), which a phone cannot open.

cj.title: Judging criteria — where to see each one in MIRGAB
cj.c1_have: Precision and recall measured on held-out phishing and legitimate links, UAE scenarios and a public SMS set (below), re-runnable live. Low false positives (0.5% on legitimate links); official country sites of banks and brands are not flagged. Evasion handled: link shorteners, redirect wrappers (unwrapped without opening), defanged links, look-alike letters, punycode, @-tricks — with its own evasion test below.
cj.c1_gap: cloaking that shows different content to scanners can't be judged without opening the page, which MIRGAB never does.
cj.c2_have: Live Radar follows Certificate Transparency logs — new HTTPS sites appear minutes after their certificate is issued, before anyone reports them — plus five public threat feeds, look-alike and brand-impersonation detection, newly registered domains (registration age in the evidence pack) and campaign linking.
cj.c2_gap: search-engine ads and Maps listings need provider APIs; they are on the roadmap.
cj.c3_have: Every result has a 0–100 score, the reasons with the exact quoted words, what to do now, and the measured reliability. For links, the evidence & takedown pack adds registration (RDAP/WHOIS), registrar, hosting network, abuse contacts, UTC timestamps and a SHA-256 fingerprint, with a ready takedown letter and JSON. Live Radar exports PDF/CSV reports.
cj.c3_gap: page screenshots, because MIRGAB never opens suspicious sites (a sandboxed browser is a roadmap item).
cj.c4_have: Arabic, Emirati dialect and English; impersonation of UAE banks, TAMM, UAE PASS, ICP, MOI, Abu Dhabi & Dubai Police, RTA/Salik traffic fines, DEWA, Etisalat/du and more. Innovations: scam domains linked into campaigns (Scam Campaign DNA), live Call Guardian, quote-grounded LLM layer, deepfake provenance scan.
cj.c5_have: Working live demo installable on phones (no App Store), push alerts, multi-user, 230+ automated tests, security-hardened. Pilot path: radar and evidence packs feed police triage; verified warnings are published only after two-person review.
cj.c5_gap: a fixed cloud address and police system integration are the next steps.
